I found two bugs in the uncommitted change to `model/features.py`, both on line 14. I only read the code and didn't run it.

1. **Test data leaks into training.** `build_features` standardizes using the mean and std of the whole DataFrame. `train.py` calls it before `train_test_split`, so the test rows influence the scaling. The reported test AUC will be slightly optimistic. The training statistics also aren't saved anywhere. A serving call on new data would compute its own mean and std, so the features wouldn't match what the model was trained on. The fix is to fit a scaler on the training split only, for example a `StandardScaler` in a sklearn `Pipeline`, and reuse it for test and inference.

2. **Zero or NaN std isn't handled.** A constant column, or a frame with a single row, gives a std of 0 or NaN. Dividing by it produces NaN or inf features, and `LogisticRegression.fit` then raises a `ValueError`. `StandardScaler` handles zero variance, which is another reason to use it.

findings.summary: Standardization uses mean/std computed over the whole DataFrame inside build_features, which runs before train_test_split, so test-set statistics leak into training.
findings.failure_scenario: train.py calls build_features(load(path)) on all rows, then splits 80/20. The scaler's mean and std include the test rows, so the reported test AUC is optimistically biased. Any inference-time call to build_features on a single row or small batch would compute its own mean/std instead (std of one row is NaN, giving all-NaN features), and nothing persists the training statistics, so the scaling can't be reproduced in serving.
findings.short_summary: Scaling fit on full data before split leaks test stats

findings.summary: Division by .std() has no guard for zero or NaN std, so a constant column or a single-row input yields NaN/inf features.
findings.failure_scenario: If a numeric column is constant (e.g. support_tickets all 0) or the frame has one row, std() is 0 or NaN, so the column becomes NaN/inf and LogisticRegression.fit raises ValueError on the NaN input.
findings.short_summary: No guard for zero/NaN std in standardization
